metadata.creator: Upham, Alfred H.
metadata.description: Alfred H. Upham, president of Miami University, writes to Murray Sheehan at the Royal Thai Legation in Washington, D.C. Upham expresses pleasure that Sheehan will attend Commencement, states that a reservation has been made for him in David Smiling Hall, and regrets that no boy from Thailand will be in the graduating class and that the Minister could not be secured as speaker.
metadata.title: Letter to Murray Sheehan from Alfred H. Upham, 26 May 1942
metadata.transcript:
[page 1]
May 26, 1942

Mr. [Mister] Murray Sheehan
Royal Thai Legation
2300 Kalorama Road
Washington, D. C. [District of Columbia]

Dear Murray [Murray Sheehan]:

I am delighted to know that you are coming on for Commencement. We shall all be glad to see you and I think you will find yourself very comfortable in David Smiling Hall where we are making a reservation for you.

It is too bad that we cannot have at least one boy from Thailand in the graduating class while you are here, particularly since we were unable to secure the Minister as our speaker.

Cordially yours,

President
